items.title: Prabowo hits back at countries 'insulting' Indonesia over wildfire haze
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's president railed Wednesday against "countries that like to insult" his nation over wildfires that have razed vast areas, spewing toxic haze into neighbouring countries. "As for certain countries that like to insult the Indonesian nation, when the time comes, we will reveal the companies involved" Prabowo told a cabinet meeting Wednesday, claiming that "many corporations bear responsibility" for the crisis. "Indonesia is a polite and patient nation.

items.title: Indonesians sue government over wildfires, haze and public health crisis
items.summary: PONTIANAK: Residents of Indonesian Borneo urged the government on Wednesday to do more to combat the wildfires consuming vast tracts of land and emitting a foul haze that has sickened thousands and curtailed daily life for months. "The issue... is not merely about burning forests and land, it is also closely tied to public health, air quality, economic activity, education and the safety of residents," resident Achmad Mundzirin told AFP in Pontianak. Lawyers have filed a class action case claiming "negligence, omission and failure" on the part of the government that has resulted in "a massive public health crisis" in West Kalimantan.

items.title: Police bust Geng Suria linked to 20 armed robberies in Kedah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have crippled an organised crime group known as Geng Suria, which was active in armed robberies across Kedah, following a special operation last month. Federal Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar S Muthuvelu said the integrated operation, conducted in collaboration with the Kedah police contingent's Criminal Investigation Department, was carried out in Kedah and Perak from Sept 24 to 27. He said the group was led by a 30-year-old man and had nine members aged between 28 and 52.

items.title: Turkiye, Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia sign defence cooperation accord
items.summary: ANKARA: Turkiye, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said. "The agreement holds substantial economic importance," it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development. Ankara also has close ties with Indonesia, notably in the defence industry.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Wednesday, October 21, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1560881]] [[nid:1560880]] [[nid:1560879]] [[nid:1560878]] [[nid:1560877]] [[nid:1560876]] [[nid:1560875]] [[nid:1560874]] [[nid:1560873]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Viral school fight video shows June incident classified NFA
items.summary: BENTONG: A viral video showing a fight involving students and adults outside a school here depicts an incident in June that police have classified as no further action (NFA). Acting Bentong police chief Deputy Superintendent Azmi Mahmod said the 31-second video resurfaced on Facebook yesterday. "Police arrested two boys, aged 15 and 16, on the same day.

items.title: IRDA appoints Ashari Kasnan as chief executive, effective Nov 1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) has announced the appointment of Datuk Ashari Kasnan as its chief executive, effective Nov 1, 2026, succeeding Datuk Mohd Noorazam Osman who has served since Jan 1, 2025. In a statement today, IRDA said this appointment marks a new chapter in IRDA's leadership as Iskandar Malaysia builds on two decades of regional development and advances its next phase of growth. "Ashari's appointment comes as Iskandar Malaysia moves beyond its 20th anniversary in 2026 and enters its next phase of regional development.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 21, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Stop using Waze Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered civil servants to stop using Waze over concerns that sensitive government information and personal data could be exploited by Israel. Shuhaily charged Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain pleaded not guilty to two charges of voluntarily causing hurt to two Special Branch policemen. Akmal auctions assets Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh is auctioning his motorcycle and farmed tilapia to raise RM300,000 to pay Teresa Kok following a defamation suit.

items.title: Haze or ship fumes? Maritime experts want closer watch on vessel emissions at Malaysian ports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Authorities should examine how much ship emissions contribute to air pollution around major ports, particularly during haze episodes originating from Indonesia, says maritime industry expert Datuk Seri Jeyenderan M. Ramasamy. Jeyenderan, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, said Malaysia’s strategic location along the Strait of Malacca, one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, offered significant opportunities to develop its marine fuel supply sector, but environmental considerations should not be overlooked. The environmental impact of shipping activity deserves closer attention, particularly when transboundary haze affects Malaysia,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Encorp wins Felda job to build staff housing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Encorp Bhd's subsidiary Encorp Construction & Engineering Sdn Bhd has secured a RM16.96 million contract to build staff housing for its major shareholder Federal Land Development Authority (Felda). Felda, through Felda Investment Corp Sdn Bhd, holds a 67.13 per cent stake in Encorp. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: 10-month-old boy died from 'blunt force' head injuries
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: A 10-month-old boy who was found weak at his babysitter's home died from head injuries consistent with blunt force trauma, police said Seberang Prai Utara district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Abdul Rahman said doctors could not determine whether the injuries were caused by an accident or another person's actions. "The medical findings showed that the victim died from head injuries consistent with blunt force trauma. Doctors also confirmed that the injuries could have been fatal," he said when contacted.

items.title: eBay to lay off 9pct of workforce in push to simplify operations, internal memo shows
items.summary: A spokesperson for eBay confirmed the layoffs to Reuters on Wednesday. The move will eliminate around 1,100 jobs, based on the 12,300 employees eBay had at the end of last year. Shares of eBay were down 1.8 per cent in premarket trading.

items.title: Waze ban: MPs ask if WhatsApp, Instagram pose similar security risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The government has been urged to provide a detailed explanation of the rationale behind the ban on the use of the Waze navigation app by civil servants, as well as the risk levels associated with other popular applications. Chow Yu Hui (PH-Raub) said that the ban on Waze, over concerns that location data could be exposed to Israel, warranted clarification, particularly regarding how its security risks differed from those of other popular US-owned applications, such as WhatsApp and Instagram. Moreover, the US government supports Israel.

items.title: Speaker awaits clarification on PN deregistration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The status and position of Perikatan Nasional (PN) MPs in the opposition bloc will be determined after parliament receives clarification on the coalition's deregistration. Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said a decision could not be finalised pending clarification from PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar. I have also written to the PN chairman (Ahmad Samsuri).

items.title: Ditch Waze, NSC tells Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Security Council (NSC) has called on civil servants and Malaysians to switch from navigation application Waze to locally developed alternatives, saying security risks involving Israel cannot be compromised. The NSC said the government took seriously the collection of users' location data, movement patterns, travel information and device details by Waze. "The government takes seriously the collection of users' location data, movement patterns, travel information and device details by navigation application Waze, particularly as its Terms of Use provide for the application of Israeli law and the jurisdiction of Israeli regime courts in disputes relating to the use of its services.

items.title: Sarawak announces two months’ salary aid for state civil servants, RM700 for federal staff
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — The Sarawak government today announced a Special Financial Assistance (BKK) equivalent to two months’ salary for state civil servants, as well as a payment of RM700 for federal civil servants serving in Sarawak. “This assistance is expected to benefit 19,851 Sarawak civil servants, with an estimated expenditure of RM144 million,” he said while concluding the debate on the 2027 State Budget at the State Legislative Assembly sitting here today. For federal civil servants in Sarawak, he announced a one-off payment of RM700.

items.title: Sarawak civil servants to receive two months' salary in special aid
items.summary: KUCHING: Sarawak will pay state civil servants special financial assistance equivalent to two months' salary in recognition of their contributions to the state's development. He said the payment was expected to benefit about 19,851 state civil servants, with an allocation of RM144 million. The state government also announced a one-off payment of RM700 for federal civil servants serving in Sarawak.

items.title: No casualties after ceiling collapses at Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital’s emergency dept in Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 21 — No patients or hospital staff were involved in a ceiling collapse incident at the Emergency and Trauma Department of Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR) in Klang yesterday, the Selangor State Health Department (JKNS) said. The incident occurred at 7.15pm along the pathway in front of the department’s Blue Zone. The department said it remained committed to prioritising the safety of patients, visitors and healthcare workers.

items.title: Macron takes aim at Trump for using France riots for election gain
items.summary: PARIS: President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday took an apparent swipe at counterpart Donald Trump of exploiting France's riots for advantage in the US midterm election battle, as Paris prepared for more protests this weekend. France's government has admitted it "lost control" in the frenzy of street violence that erupted last weekend, when masked youths clashed with police, looted shops and vandalised public buildings. Several analysts have dismissed the claims that migrants were driving France's protests.

items.title: Malakoff names Aznita Abdul Aziz as director, Nurshazwani Abd Malek as covering CFO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malakoff Corp Bhd has appointed Aznita Abdul Aziz as an independent non-executive director effective today. Aznita brings about 26 years of experience in the oil and gas industry, primarily with the Petronas group, covering risk management, strategic planning, portfolio management, treasury operations and economic evaluation. Separately, Malakoff appointed deputy chief financial officer Nurshazwani Abd Malek as covering chief financial officer from Dec 1.

items.title: Eonmetall shares to be suspended from Nov 4 ahead of delisting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Trading of Eonmetall Group Bhd (EGB) shares on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia will be suspended with effect from 9am on Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026. Eonmetall said the trading of EGB shares will continue to be suspended until the delisting of EGB from the official list of Bursa Malaysia following the completion of the selective capital reduction (SCR). The cash consideration is RM0.45 for each EGB share held on the entitlement date.

items.title: MPs call for stronger school safety measures after Kuching attack
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Incidents involving the safety of students and teachers should no longer be treated as isolated cases, given their repeated occurrence in recent years, said Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching). He said the latest incident involving a student at an international school in Kuching had heightened concerns among parents and students about school safety. he said.

items.title: Oil prices jump US$2 as Iran dents hopes of diplomatic progress
items.summary: LONDON: Oil prices jumped more than US$2 on Wednesday after Iran said there was little reason to expect diplomatic progress with the United States, leaving Brent crude near five-month highs, with further support from falling US crude and fuel inventories. Brent crude futures gained US$2.06, or 1.9 per cent, to US$110.85 a barrel by 1048 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose US$2.13, or 2.2 per cent, to US$99.95.

items.title: Prabowo accuses MSCI of trying to intimidate Indonesia after market rout
items.summary: JAKARTA: Global index provider MSCI was trying to "intimidate" Indonesia, but the country would not be afraid, President Prabowo Subianto told his Cabinet on Wednesday in his first public response to last week's downgrade warning. "MSCI will continue to monitor developments in the Indonesian market and engage with market participants and authorities," it said. Other senior Indonesian political figures have also reacted strongly to MSCI's warning.

items.title: Malaysia’s consumer empowerment index rises to 70.36pc from 63.1pc in 2020
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysian consumers’ empowerment level has improved from moderate to high, with the 2025 Consumer Empowerment Index (CEI) recording an overall score of 70.36 per cent, up from 63.1 per cent in 2020. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the increase of 7.26 percentage points reflected consumers’ growing knowledge, confidence and ability to make informed decisions and take action to protect their rights. The Purchase Decision domain improved by 7.11 percentage points to 75.91 per cent, while the Financial Literacy domain rose by 3.97 percentage points to 66.47 per cent.

items.title: Kelantan police enlist community leaders in fight against drugs
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: Kelantan police will enlist community leaders and members of the public to strengthen efforts to combat drug abuse and trafficking in the state. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said police welcomed information and cooperation from the public to support ongoing efforts to tackle the drug problem. Yusoff said Kelantan police declared war on drugs in 2024 to instil a stronger commitment among personnel to combat the problem.

items.title: MAHB to deploy K9 units at KLIA from Oct 26 amid heightened drug smuggling scrutiny
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd will deploy K9 patrol units inside the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) terminals on Oct 26, amid heightened scrutiny over recent transnational drug smuggling cases originating from the airport. Managing Director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said the deployment will cover passenger-facing areas such as the departure hall, arrival hall and customs inspection areas, enabling early detection of prohibited items and potential security threats linked to targeted flights. Earlier, KLIA police chief ACP M. Ravi said police had stepped up K9 patrols, previously conducted periodically, to bolster airport security following several recent incidents.

items.title: Pantech Global's Q2 earnings soar 90pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pantech Global Bhd's net profit soared 89.5 per cent to RM19.33 million in the second quarter ended Aug 31, 2026 (Q2 FY27), from RM10.2 million a year earlier. Pantech's quarterly revenue increased 36.9 per cent to RM173.71 million from RM126.9 million a year earlier, driven by higher sales volume and improved average selling prices. For the first half of FY27, Pantech's net profit increased 60.6 per cent to RM35.69 million from RM22.23 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 32 per cent to RM333.39 million from RM252.53 million.

items.title: Selangor ketum raid nets 27 men, including three civil servants
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH, Oct 21 — Three civil servants were among 27 men detained in a raid on a premises believed to be involved in the sale and processing of ketum leaves and water here today. Commenting further, Zainudin said the premises also offered cough syrup based on customer requests, which is believed to be used for mixing with ketum water. He said the seized materials, including ketum leaves and ketum water, will be handed over for further investigation in collaboration with the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters (IPD).

items.title: Locals swoop in to shield foreign operators in Klang business crackdown
items.summary: KLANG: Several Malaysians turned up claiming to be employers or caretakers of business premises during an immigration crackdown on businesses suspected of being operated by or employing foreigners in Meru here today. The situation unfolded at several premises inspected during a joint operation by the Selangor Immigration Department and Klang Royal City Council (MBDK), which began at 11am. At one premises, a Bangladeshi man believed to be the employer became agitated when MBDK enforcement officers inspected his shop.

items.title: CapitaLand Malaysia's net profit rises to RM47.02mil in Q3
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CapitaLand Malaysia Trust's net profit for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026) rose to RM47.02 million from RM34.69 million in the same quarter a year ago. "Property operating expenses rose marginally by RM200,000, or 0.4 per cent, to RM47.1 million against 3Q 2025. For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026 (9M 2026), its net profit rose to RM136.82 million from RM107.24 million, while revenue climbed to RM376.98 million from RM352.14 million previously.

items.title: 59 undocumented foreigners arrested in Penang raids
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Some 59 undocumented foreigners were arrested in Immigration Department raids at four premises in Bukit Mertajam and Prai. They comprised 14 Vietnamese, nine Thais, six Indonesians, four Chinese citizens and two Laotians. They comprised five Myanmar citizens, five Nepalese, six Chinese citizens, three Sri Lankans, two Bangladeshis and one Indian.

items.title: Police arrest male student over alleged axe, penknife attack on teacher at Kuching international school
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — A male Form Four student was arrested after he allegedly attacked a female teacher at an international school here, injuring her this morning. Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak confirmed the incident, that occurred at about 8am, adding that a penknife and a small axe were found. “Further details about the incident will be made by the Kuching district police chief,” he said in a statement today, adding that the student has been released on police bail.

items.title: Malaysia proposes high-level committee with Indonesia to boost creative industry ties
items.summary: JAKARTA, Oct 21 — Malaysia has proposed establishing a cross-ministerial High-Level Committee (HLC) with Indonesia to accelerate bilateral cooperation in the creative industries and creative economy. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that the committee would facilitate discussions on collaborative initiatives, including those that could be formalised through memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with relevant Indonesian ministries. He said that the proposed mechanism would also help coordinate cooperation across different ministerial portfolios, as areas overseen by Malaysia’s Communications Ministry fell under several ministries in Indonesia, including those responsible for culture, communications and the creative economy.

items.title: Indonesian woman arrested over illegal immigration services promoted on TikTok
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: An Indonesian woman suspected of using TikTok to promote illegal immigration services, including arranging migrant movements through unauthorised routes, has been arrested following a month-long intelligence operation. Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation, which began at 10am, was carried out by officers from the department's Intelligence and Special Operations Division at its headquarters in Putrajaya. Zakaria said investigations revealed that the woman had used TikTok to advertise immigration-related services targeting Indonesians living in the Klang Valley.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 21, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended marginally higher, reclaiming the 1,600 psychological level as bargain hunting provided support amid cautious sentiment. In the crypto market, Bitcoin rose to RM340,484. HC7XzSoRJME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: More than 20 Bangladeshi passports found at Meru business premises
items.summary: KLANG: More than 20 Bangladeshi passports were found at a business premises in Meru here today, prompting an investigation into why the travel documents were being kept there. Checks uncovered dozens of foreign passports, including several kept in a locked safe. Selangor acting Immigration director Mohmad Khusairi Kamarudin said more than 20 Bangladeshi passports containing valid particulars were found during the inspection.

items.title: Langkawi ferry runs aground off Kuala Perlis, all 251 passengers evacuated
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 21 — A total of 251 passengers aboard the Express Bahagia 98 (EB98) ferry from Langkawi, which ran aground on a sandbank near the entrance to the Kuala Perlis Passenger Ferry Terminal this morning, were safely evacuated at 2.50 pm today. “The evacuation operation was carried out in collaboration with the Kuala Perlis Marine Police, the Kuala Perlis Fishermen’s Association and Sea Splash Travel Sdn Bhd after two initial attempts to tow the ferry using Feri Kenangan 6 and Langkawi Auto Express 1 failed due to the falling sea level,” he said in a statement today. Norhafiz said the EB98 ferry departed Langkawi at 9.30am before running aground at about 10.35am near Buoy No 1 in Kuala Perlis, when the captain took evasive action to avoid a fishing net stretched across the inbound and outbound shipping channel at Kuala Perlis.

items.title: Sunway Healthcare, Putrajaya Holdings to build 325-bed hospital
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd and Putrajaya Holdings Sdn Bhd have formalised a 60:40 joint venture to develop a 325-bed multi-specialty private hospital in Putrajaya. The proposed Sunway Medical Centre Putrajaya, which will offer tertiary healthcare and specialist services, is expected to be completed in 2031, subject to the relevant approvals and project timelines. Their respective wholly-owned subsidiaries Sunway Healthcare Ventures Sdn Bhd and Tapak Senja Sdn Bhd signed the definitive joint venture and shareholders agreement, following a heads of agreement signed on April 23, 2025.

items.title: More than 3,000 attend Selangor Sultan’s Silver Jubilee royal tea reception in Klang
items.summary: KLANG, 21 Oct — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, graced a Royal Tea Reception with over 3,000 citizens in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of his reign at Istana Alam Shah here today. The Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin and the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah, were also in attendance. Their Royal Highnesses were welcomed upon arrival by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin.

items.title: Kelantan orders data collection on Myanmar refugees across all districts
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 21 — The Kelantan government has instructed all district officers to collect data on the number and locations of Myanmar refugees throughout the state as a preparatory step to address issues related to the community. State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said that so far, the state government has only received data from the Tanah Merah district, which recorded about 80 families involving more than 300 individuals, in Kampung Padang Guchil, who cultivate betel leaves over an area of two hectares. Commenting on the jurisdiction of the state government, Hilmi said the state’s powers are limited to matters related to land and premises, including illegal encroachment of government land, violations of private land use conditions, and compliance with business licences under the local authority (PBT).

items.title: Police probe alleged axe attack on teacher by 16-year-old boy at Sarawak international school
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — Police are investigating a 16-year-old male student for allegedly attacking a teacher with an axe at an international school here today. Acting Sarawak Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said police received a report of the incident at 8.03am via the MERS 999 emergency line. He said the report alleged that a student had brought firecrackers and used an axe to injure a teacher.

items.title: Haze: Schools in KL, Putrajaya and five states to open tomorrow, outdoor activities suspended
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Schools in the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, and Penang, will operate as usual tomorrow; however, all outdoor activities have been postponed due to the haze. In Kuala Lumpur, the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Education Department announced that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) will conduct in-person classes as usual, even though all outdoor activities are to be postponed. In Selangor, the State Education Department (JPN) announced that all educational institutions under its purview will operate as usual.

items.title: Immigration Dept raids 19 locations in Janda Baik, detains 65 foreigners
items.summary: BENTONG, Oct 21 — The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) raided 19 locations around Janda Baik in a Mega Integrated Operation this morning and detained 65 foreign nationals for various immigration offences. Its deputy director-general (Operations), Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli, said the operation which began at 10am and covered Kampung Cemeruh, Kampung Ceringin and Kampung Sumsum, was conducted following complaints from residents and media reports about the influx of foreign nationals in the resort area. Lokman Effendi said the integrated operation involved 150 JIM members from Pahang, Kuala Lummpur and the Putrajaya headquarters, in addition to the cooperation of the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and the National Registration Department (JPN).

items.title: Malaysia reviews framework for technical aid to developing countries amid global challenges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry is reviewing ways to strengthen the institutional framework for the country’s international development cooperation to better support developing countries grappling with mounting debt, escalating conflicts and the threat of a widening technological divide. Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said the review would draw on insights from a symposium on the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme (MTCP), a key instrument of Malaysia’s commitment to developing countries through human capital development, technical assistance and capacity building. Under the 12th Malaysia Plan (2021-2025), he said the MTCP funded 330 capacity-building programmes benefiting 5,609 participants from 144 developing countries, while supporting 87 scholars pursuing tertiary education in Malaysia.

items.title: MCMC records statement of individual over Facebook content allegedly insulting Negeri Sembilan royal institution
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Oct 21 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has recorded the statement of an individual to assist in an investigation into Facebook content suspected of containing elements insulting the Negeri Sembilan royal institution. In a statement today, MCMC said the action was taken to complete an investigation under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588). MCMC is investigating content uploaded through the Facebook account “Che GuBard”, which is suspected of containing elements insulting the Negeri Sembilan royal institution, as well as touching on the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and members of the Negeri Sembilan royal family.

items.title: Home Ministry: Govt has no plans to amend citizenship law for children born before parents’ marriage registration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The government has no plans to amend Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution, which governs the citizenship status of children born before their parents’ marriage is legally registered. Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the provision remains relevant to ensure that citizenship is determined in accordance with existing laws. For children born before their parents’ marriage is legally registered, Shamsul Anuar said the child’s citizenship status is determined by the citizenship status of the biological mother, in line with Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: Home minister: Malaysia, Japan to strengthen cooperation to combat transnational crime
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia and Japan are committed to strengthening security cooperation to combat transnational crime through information sharing and investigative collaboration between the Royal Malaysia Police and the National Police Agency (NPA) of Japan. He said the discussions focused on expanding information sharing and strengthening investigative cooperation to combat drug trafficking, cybercrime, online scams and human trafficking. “Transnational crime recognises no national boundaries.

items.title: Sarawak police probe Kuching school incident that left teacher injured
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — Sarawak police are investigating an incident in which a 16-year-old male student allegedly injured a female teacher with an axe at a private school here this morning. Sarawak acting police commissioner Datuk Saifullizan Ishak said police received information about the incident through the MERS 999 emergency line at about 8.03am today, after the Kuching district police headquarters control centre was alerted to a student allegedly carrying firecrackers and injuring a teacher. He said police were conducting a detailed investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and gather relevant evidence.

items.title: PMO confirms civil servants barred from using Waze over Israel data security risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The federal government barred all civil servants from using the Waze navigation application over concerns that sensitive official data and users’ personal information could be harvested and exploited by Israel, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) confirmed today. In a statement, the PMO confirmed that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered an immediate ban across the public sector to safeguard government data and citizens’ movement information. “Sensitive government information and the personal data of the people must be protected from being exploited by the Israeli regime in ways that could compromise national security and sovereignty,” the statement read.

items.title: PM Anwar expresses concern over Middle East conflict, condemns Houthi attacks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia continues to view with great concern the dangerous escalation of conflict unfolding across the Middle East, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said that he has been in close contact with key regional leaders, including Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed Salman and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed Abdulrahman Al Thani. He emphasised that this same moral conviction compels Malaysia to speak out with equal firmness whenever innocent civilians are targeted anywhere else.

items.title: Malaysian Bar, office-bearers awarded RM59,499 after winning part of appeal over 2022 independence march
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 21 —The Court of Appeal today partly allowed the Malaysian Bar’s appeal over its 2022 Walk for Judicial Independence, awarding RM59,499 in damages to the Bar and four of its office-bearers for violating their constitutional rights in connection with the march. The march was held on June 17, 2022, to protest the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) public announcement of an investigation into then Court of Appeal judge Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali, now a Federal Court judge. On March 20 last year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court held that the police had acted ultra vires (beyond their powers) by imposing conditions prohibiting the march, but awarded the Bar only RM1 in nominal damages, a sum proposed by the Bar’s counsel.

items.title: Johari: Malaysia’s chip talent retention remains sustainable despite foreign offers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Starting salaries for junior engineers and technicians in the local chip industry scale up steadily with experience, offering sustainable career progression even as overseas markets tempt local talent with higher pay, said Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today. Johari acknowledged the salaries may seem nominally low when compared to what companies in countries like Taiwan or South Korea may offer, but said they must still weigh higher overseas pay against the increased cost of living in those countries. “If compared with job offers overseas in places like the UK, Singapore, Korea, or Taiwan, salaries might be two to three times higher,” Johari said during Question Time.

items.title: Loke envisions Transport Expo Asia rivalling LIMA as regional mobility showcase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke hopes the biennial Transport Expo Asia (TXA) will develop into a premier international showcase on par with the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA), drawing top global exhibitors and industry investors to Malaysia. Loke said that the event serves as an ideal launchpad to spotlight progress across land transport, aviation, maritime, and logistics sectors, placing particular emphasis on emerging technologies like autonomous driving, robotics, and unmanned aerial systems. “We certainly hope this will help drive growth in the transport sector through greater strategic cooperation,” he said.

items.title: Sarawak completes integrated rare earth elements roadmap to build ‘super magnet’ industry, says Awang Tengah
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — The Sarawak government has completed an integrated framework for the development of the rare earth elements (REE) industry, covering the entire value chain from upstream to downstream activities, said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan. The Second Natural Resources and Urban Development Minister said the Sarawak REE Industry Development Roadmap aims to develop a ‘super magnet’ industry to support the growth of Sarawak’s semiconductor, aerospace, and satellite industries, in addition to applications in electric vehicle manufacturing, defence technology, medicine, and other sectors. On a related matter, Awang Tengah said the Sarawak Minerals Management Authority (SMMA) has approved the Sarawak Mineral Industry Development Policy, which comprises seven pillars and 43 key components.

items.title: Teacher injured while disarming student in Kuching school
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — A teacher was injured while attempting to wrest a sharp object from a student at an international school here this morning. It is learned that the secondary school student was brought under control and taken to the principal’s office before the police arrived and took over the matter. Kuching district police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu, when contacted, said the police are looking into the incident.

items.title: KLIA deploys K9 sniffer dog units to tighten airport security and curb smuggling
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 21 — Trained sniffer dog units will begin patrolling passenger terminals and restricted baggage zones across KL International Airport (KLIA) from Oct 26, Malaysia Airports announced today. The airport operator described the deployment as a multi-layered security strategy that shields public passenger-facing concourses while reinforcing back-of-house operations alongside existing surveillance architecture. Malaysia Airports managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said integrating canine units into daily operations strengthens inter-agency vigilance to safeguard international travellers, visitors, and airport staff, while freeing airport Aviation Security (AVSEC) teams to concentrate on their primary protective functions.

items.title: No more ‘kindergarten colours’: DBKL opts for neutral tones in RM446m public housing facelift
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The capital’s public housing schemes are receiving a major aesthetic and safety facelift, with City Hall (DBKL) foregoing garish paint schemes for neutral tones while overhauling critical electrical infrastructure across dozens of ageing buildings. Speaking during a working visit to People’s Housing Programme (PPR) Taman Mulia in Bandar Tun Razak today, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said that DBKL made a deliberate shift away from the bright, multi-coloured exteriors long associated with government flats. At PPR Taman Mulia, DBKL committed RM6.67 million in restorative works for roughly 2,128 residents.

items.title: Malaysians who lend MyKad to foreigners face up to three years’ jail, says Home Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Individuals who misuse their identity cards (MyKad) by ‘renting out’ or handing them over to foreign nationals could face up to three years in prison, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both, Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said. He said the National Registration Regulations 1990 provide strict legal measures to curb foreign nationals’ misuse of national identity. Shamsul Anuar said the operation underscored the importance of joint enforcement efforts by the National Registration Department (NRD), the Immigration Department and Labour Department.

items.title: Find another way: Civil servants effectively banned from using Waze app due to Israel ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Civil servants have been banned from using the Waze navigation app with immediate effect, following a decision by the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) at its meeting yesterday. In a letter dated October 20, Chief Secretary to the Government (KSN) Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the JKSN Meeting No. 3 of 2026 was chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
